title: BAGMAN XeroAccount
description: One synced projection of a Xero Chart-of-Accounts row (`GET /Accounts`, CD-6 Slice 2, PID §98.4, architect spec §4). Durable external identity is `(tenant_id, account_id)` — enforced as a real database-level unique constraint (`persistence/postgres/xero_models.py`), so a repeated sync of the same account UPDATES this same row rather than duplicating it (idempotency, architect spec §4/§29). `type`/`account_class`/`status`/`tax_type` are captured VERBATIM from Xero and are deliberately OPEN string fields here (never a hand-typed closed enum) — PID §102.1's own researched doctrine, matching this repository's existing 'open taxonomy field' pattern for every other provider-supplied vocabulary (`entity_type`, `evidence_type`, `source_type`, ...). An account that becomes inactive/archived in Xero is never deleted from this projection — only its `status` is updated on a later sync (architect spec §5/§6's 'retained historically, not silently deleted').

xero_account_row_id.description: Canonical BAGMAN identifier for this projection row (distinct from Xero's own `account_id`).

entity_id.description: The BAGMAN `GovernedEntity` this account belongs to (via its `XeroConnection`) — denormalised onto every row so a query for 'accounts for company X' never needs to join through the connection table, and so cross-company isolation is directly, trivially provable (a query scoped to one `entity_id` structurally cannot return another company's rows).

tenant_id.description: The Xero organisation/tenant this account belongs to (half of this row's durable external identity, together with `account_id`).

account_id.description: Xero's own `AccountID` (a Xero-minted GUID) — the other half of this row's durable external identity. This, not `code` or `name`, is what a BAGMAN record that references a Xero account actually stores (architect spec §8/§9-10's 'the stored selector value is the real AccountID, never a display string').

code.description: Xero's `Code` (e.g. `"453"`) verbatim. Xero permits a null/blank code on some account types.

type.description: Xero's `Type` verbatim (e.g. `EXPENSE`, `OVERHEADS`, `CURRENT`). Deliberately open — see this schema's own top-level description.

account_class.description: Xero's `Class` verbatim, when supplied (e.g. `EXPENSE`, `ASSET`, `REVENUE`) — PID §98.4's own 'Class if supplied'. Deliberately open. Named `account_class` (not `class`) purely because `class` is a reserved word in several languages this contract's consumers are written in; the value is Xero's `Class` field unmodified.

status.description: Xero's own `Status` verbatim (e.g. `ACTIVE`, `ARCHIVED`, `DELETED`) — deliberately open (NOT validated against a hand-typed closed set here); see `services/xero/eligibility.py` for the DOCUMENTED, separate application-layer filtering policy that reads this field to decide default dropdown visibility without ever deleting a row for it.

show_in_expense_claims.description: Xero's `ShowInExpenseClaims` verbatim. Useful eligibility-filtering signal, but NEVER the sole eligibility rule (architect spec §5/PID §98.4's explicit instruction) — see `services/xero/eligibility.py`.

source_updated_date_utc.description: Xero's own `UpdatedDateUTC` for this account — the PROVIDER's last-modified timestamp, distinct from `last_synced_at` below (BAGMAN's own fetch time).

first_synced_at.description: UTC timestamp this row was first created by a sync — immutable once set (never updated by a later sync of the same account).

last_synced_at.description: UTC timestamp of the most recent sync run that observed this exact account (updated on every idempotent re-sync, whether or not any other field actually changed).

last_sync_run_id.description: The `XeroSyncRun.sync_run_id` that most recently wrote this row — traceability back to exactly which sync attempt produced the current projection (architect spec §29's provenance requirement).
